Five of the nine input metabolites — arachidonic acid, 5-HETE, 15-HETE, leukotriene A4, and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-prostaglandin J2 — map to the eicosanoid synthesis pathway (WP:WP167) with a false-discovery rate of 1.39e-12 and a fold enrichment of 1251, as identified by multi-database over-representation analysis (RaMP-DB). react_result.final_narrative_text: The treatment group exhibits a strong perturbation of the arachidonic acid eicosanoid synthesis cascade. Five of the nine input metabolites — arachidonic acid, 5-HETE, 15-HETE, leukotriene A4, and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-prostaglandin J2 — map to the eicosanoid synthesis pathway (WP:WP167) with a false-discovery rate of 1.39e-12 and a fold enrichment of 1251, as identified by multi-database over-representation analysis (RaMP-DB). The m/z-directed mummichog algorithm independently recovered arachidonic acid metabolism as the top network-ranked pathway (p = 0.0068), hitting all four lipoxygenase-branch metabolites. KEGG-specific pathway-set enrichment (MetaboAnalystR) returned the same arachidonic acid cascade as the top hit (KEGG:hsa00590). The three cross-paradigm winners — WP:WP167, MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism, and KEGG:hsa00590 — describe the same biochemical process from different namespace perspectives. Arachidonic acid is the upstream substrate from which 5-HETE (5-LOX product), 15-HETE (15-LOX product), leukotriene A4 (5-LOX/epoxide hydrolase product), and 15-deoxy-PGJ2 (cyclooxygenase dehydration product) all derive. The convergence across ORA, network-activity, and KEGG-specific methods, with all five driver metabolites independently verified as eicosanoid-class compounds sharing the same InChIKey first-block within their respective cross-tool reconciliations, indicates a treatment-induced dysregulation of the oxidative eicosanoid branch rather than the enzymatic prostaglandin branch. Methylmalonic acid and 6-methylmercaptopurine did not contribute to the eicosanoid signal; L-serine maps only to glycerophospholipid/serine metabolism at lower significance.

final_claims.claim_text: Multi-database ORA (RaMP-DB) identified "Eicosanoid synthesis" (WP:WP167) as the top pathway with FDR = 1.39e-12 and fold enrichment 1250.9.
The m/z-directed mummichog algorithm independently recovered "Arachidonic acid metabolism" (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) as the top network-ranked pathway with p = 0.00807.
KEGG-specific pathway-set enrichment via MetaboAnalystR returned KEGG:hsa00590 as the top-ranked KEGG pathway.
5-HETE is a member compound of "Eicosanoid synthesis" (WP:WP167).
15-HETE is a member compound of "Eicosanoid synthesis" (WP:WP167).
Leukotriene A4 is a member compound of "Eicosanoid synthesis" (WP:WP167).
15-Deoxy-d-12,14-PGJ2 is a member compound of "Eicosanoid synthesis" (WP:WP167).
Arachidonic acid is a member compound of "Eicosanoid synthesis" (WP:WP167).
Arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219) serves as the upstream substrate in "Eicosanoid synthesis" (WP:WP167).

The five driver metabolites (arachidonic acid, 5-HETE, 15-HETE, leukotriene A4, and 15-deoxy-PGJ2) were identified as members of WP:WP167 and MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism, establishing the oxidative eicosanoid branch as the affected signalling node.
Mummichog additionally captured L-serine through glycerophospholipid metabolism (MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism, p = 0.0198).

The m/z-directed mummichog algorithm independently recovered arachidonic acid metabolism as the top network-ranked pathway (p = 0.0068), hitting all four lipoxygenase-branch metabolites. Arachidonic acid is the upstream substrate from which 5-HETE (5-LOX product), 15-HETE (15-LOX product), leukotriene A4 (5-LOX/epoxide hydrolase product), and 15-deoxy-PGJ2 (cyclooxygenase dehydration product) all derive.
